prompt: At a harbour the water is $9$ m deep at high tide and $3$ m deep at low tide. The depth follows a sine wave. What is the MIDLINE depth, in metres?
hint: The midline is the level the wave wiggles around — right between the highest and lowest.

hints.text: The midline is the level the wave wiggles around — right between the highest and lowest.

explanation: A tide graph is a wave: high, low, high, low, forever.
The midline sits exactly halfway between the peak and the trough, so average them.
$(9 + 3) \div 2 = 12 \div 2 = 6$ m. (The amplitude would be the half-GAP: $(9 - 3) \div 2 = 3$ m.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Climb up from the bottom
steps: The gap from low to high is 9 − 3 = 6 m.
The middle is half that gap above the low point: 3 + 3 = 6 m.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write the equation
steps: The model is depth = a·sin(x) + k, with k the midline and a the amplitude.
High = k + a = 9 and low = k − a = 3. Add the two lines: 2k = 12, so k = 6.
